answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally issued credential in an on-chain registry before it may claim rewards. The registry accepts each credential only once, while periodic challenges force the agent to prove control by signing a fresh nonce with its registered key; a copied profile or replayed cipher cannot pass. An attacker must acquire distinct credentials and lock real value for every identity, tying up capital and risking forfeiture, whether operating from an ocean platform or an onyx server farm.
